summary: This bill requires the FCC to hold annual public hearings after major disaster activations of its Disaster Information Reporting System and issue public reports detailing outages of broadband, VoIP, and mobile services along with impacts on emergency calls, then investigate and recommend rule changes to improve outage notifications to 9-1-1 centers.

scores.thoughts: The bill requires the FCC to hold annual public hearings and issue reports on disaster-related network outages. These are administrative functions that may involve minor agency resources, but the legislation does not authorize new appropriations, expand programs, or direct any change in overall federal spending levels.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection.
The bill addresses communications outage reporting for emergency services but does not engage with healthcare delivery, insurance, coverage models, or medical regulation.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill makes no reference to immigration policy, border security, visas, or related protections.
No content relates to reproductive rights, abortion access, or restrictions.
The legislation does not address military budgets, defense programs, or national security spending.

While the bill concerns disaster-related communications outages (which can include weather events), it focuses exclusively on FCC reporting requirements and does not create, expand, or limit environmental regulations or protections.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other social safety-net benefits.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation appear in the text.
The bill contains no provisions on sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
Nothing in the bill relates to tariffs, trade agreements, or protectionist measures.
The legislation does not address deficit spending, debt reduction, or fiscal policy targets.
No provisions concern legal protections or restrictions related to LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bill does not mention foreign aid, international assistance, or related funding.
No content addresses voting access, election integrity, voter ID, or electoral procedures.

The bill mandates additional FCC reporting and investigation into network outage notifications but explicitly limits new authority over broadband providers and does not address data privacy, consumer data protection, or broader tech regulation.
The legislation contains no provisions affecting worker protections, union rights, or employer obligations.
No sections address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
